marie (support): Hey team -- customer reported repeated 413s when trying to bulk upload ~200k documents to the embeddings endpoint. Posting logs and repro steps below. High priority because it's blocking their migration.

marie (support): Summary: uploads hit 413 Request Entity Too Large during a single POST with a newline-delimited JSON payload. They also saw occasional "dimension mismatch" errors when they retried with different batching. Customer wants recommended streaming/chunking pattern and guidance on service limits.

ana (customer-success): FYI customer is on hosted plan; no Dedicated. They tried compressing, but still 413s. They said each embedding vector is 1536 dims (OpenAI-style), content about 2–3KB per doc. Total upload ~350MB when batched into 10k objects.

rohan (eng-ml): Thanks. Two separate issues to address: (A) 413 means payload exceeded API gateway limit (request size) and/or an internal service limit. (B) dimension mismatch is usually caused by mixing models or performing a manual post-processing step that alters vector length.

marie (support): Here are the relevant excerpts from their client logs (sanitized):

```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings 413
{
  "error": "Request Entity Too Large",
  "message": "payload exceeds 32MB limit"
}
...retrying with batch_size=512...

HTTP 200
{"data":[{"embedding":[...1536 floats...]}]}
...feed into DB...

Later:
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings 200
Response contains: "dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1537"
```

marie (support): They said the 1537 case showed for ~12 documents out of 120k after a partial retry run.

rohan (eng-ml): That screams inconsistent client-side preprocessing. A couple of possibilities: (1) they accidentally appended metadata (e.g., a length/int token) to the vector before sending, (2) mismatch between model used for encode and the configured model param, or (3) serialization error where floats become nested array or a trailing comma parsed as an extra element.

kevin (eng-platform): For the 413 root cause: our hosted API enforces a 32MB per-request payload limit at the gateway (and an additional 10MB limit at the microservice layer for some older clusters). In practice we recommend chunking to stay under 25MB payload to allow header/overhead. For private/Dedicated customers we can relax that with config, but hosted customers should stream.

marie (support): Proposed immediate guidance to customer: stream or chunk the upload into smaller batches (e.g., 100–1000 documents depending on average doc size) and validate vector dims before POST. I'm drafting sample code, posting below.

rohan (eng-ml): Please include a deterministic dim check before upload and a retry policy that avoids re-merging partial failed batches in a way that duplicates or corrupts vectors. Also include idempotency key per document or per mini-batch.

marie (support): Sample chunked upload pattern (curl + python pseudo):

```
# pseudo curl pattern, newline-delimited JSON (ndjson)
# chunk files into <= 20MB pieces and POST sequentially
for chunk in chunks/*.ndjson; do
  curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/x-ndjson" \
    --data-binary @$chunk
done
```

# Python streaming example using generator + requests
import json
import requests

API = "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}", "Content-Type": "application/x-ndjson"}

def chunked_ndjson(docs, max_bytes=20_000_000):
    buf = []
    size = 0
    for d in docs:
        line = json.dumps(d) + "\n"
        if size + len(line.encode('utf-8')) > max_bytes and buf:
            yield ''.join(buf)
            buf = []
            size = 0
        buf.append(line)
        size += len(line.encode('utf-8'))
    if buf:
        yield ''.join(buf)

for part in chunked_ndjson(generator_of_documents()):
    r = requests.post(API, headers=HEADERS, data=part)
    r.raise_for_status()
```

marie (support): Key things in the sample: NDJSON avoids a giant JSON array and allows streaming; limit each part to ~20MB to be safe; validate dims locally before sending.

ana (customer-success): Customer asked about "chunked Transfer-Encoding: chunked" streaming vs multipart POSTs. Which do we support?

kevin (eng-platform): For hosted API we accept chunked Transfer-Encoding for streaming requests to the v1/embeddings endpoint, but we do not allow arbitrary infinite streams — the endpoint will still enforce a max request size and a per-request timeout (we recommend <=60s). In practice using NDJSON and sending bounded chunks (as above) is the simplest and most robust. Multipart is fine but adds complexity; NDJSON keeps the server parsing simple.

rohan (eng-ml): On the dimension mismatch: add this check before enqueueing to any chunk send: assert len(vector) == EXPECTED_DIM and all(isinstance(x, (float, int)) for x in vector). If you use numpy, ensure to cast to native python floats or tolist() before json encoding. Example check: 

```
EXPECTED_DIM = 1536
if len(v) != EXPECTED_DIM:
    # log doc id and skip/repair
    logger.warn(f"dim mismatch for id={doc['id']}: {len(v)}")
```

marie (support): The customer also reported a performance issue when they reduced batch_size to 128: the throughput dropped from ~3k docs/s to ~400 docs/s (they were on shared hosted plan). Any guidance?

rohan (eng-ml): Throughput depends on effective batching and internal continuous batching in the runtime. Small client-side batches reduce throughput because each request hits the scheduler. For embeddings, try to maximize per-request parallelism while staying under payload limits. Observations: 1) for dense 1536-d vectors, target 1–2MB per request at minimum for good GPU efficiency 2) use concurrency of 4–8 parallel requests rather than tiny serial requests 3) for highest throughput recommend Dedicated with higher concurrency or the bulk ingest API if available.

kevin (eng-platform): I'll check telemetry for their region and customer token for gateway 413s and for any internal 10MB microservice quotas. If we see repeated 413 at the gateway we can route to an alternate edge that supports larger request window.

sre-bot: Incident check summary: no platform-wide regression. Gateway rule applied: max_request_size=32_000_000 for hosted-prod-edge-3. No recent changes.

marie (support): Repro steps to provide to customer (concise):
1) Run local dim-check on all produced vectors and fail fast on mismatches. Save list of failed ids.
2) Produce NDJSON with one object per line, each object: {"id":..., "input":..., "embedding": [...]} or if you are sending raw inputs use {"input":"..."} and let API compute embedding.
3) Chunk NDJSON into <=20MB parts. Use curl or requests.post with data=part or send as chunked but bounded.
4) Add idempotency id per doc or per-chunk so retries are safe.
5) For throughput, use concurrency (threadpool) of ~4–8 POSTs in parallel, tune by observed latency.

marie (support): Example minimal NDJSON object for server-side encoding: {"id":"doc-1234","text":"..."}
Example object when uploading pre-computed vectors: {"id":"doc-1234","embedding":[0.001,0.12,...]}

rohan (eng-ml): If they are precomputing embeddings offline, also ensure consistent dtype and normalization. For example, quantization or float16->float32 conversions can sometimes change representation if they're serializing with a library that truncates or serializes as strings. Prefer JSON arrays of floats.

ana (customer-success): Customer asked about partial failure handling: they want to continue ingesting good chunks while logging bad docs for later manual fix. Any server-side guarantees?

kevin (eng-platform): The API responds per-request. If a chunk contains a malformed entry the entire chunk may be rejected with 4xx. So best practice: pre-validate client-side and send smaller chunks so bad records are isolated. If they need per-record success/fail semantics, they can use a pattern where each line returns an explicit acceptance or error per id and you reconcile. We'll add this as a note in the docs.

marie (support): Action items: (1) send this guidance and code snippets to customer (ANA), (2) rohan: provide a small dim-check snippet that logs example offending vectors and common causes, (3) kevin: check gateway logs for token X-REDACTED to see whether the 413s map to the 32MB limit or internal 10MB microservice limit.

rohan (eng-ml): Dim-check snippet (python):
```
EXPECTED_DIM = 1536
bad = []
for doc in docs:
    v = doc.get('embedding')
    if v is None:
        continue
    if not isinstance(v, list) or len(v) != EXPECTED_DIM:
        bad.append(doc['id'])
    else:
        # type check
        for x in v:
            if not isinstance(x, (float, int)):
                bad.append(doc['id'])
                break
# persist bad ids for manual review
```

rohan (eng-ml): If they need a server-side tolerant ingest we can consider an endpoint variant that accepts streaming and returns a per-line status (like a bulk-upload job API). That's a product ask; file a ticket if they need it.

kevin (eng-platform): Checked logs for token X-REDACTED: three requests matched size ~340MB (they were sending 10k objects in a single request). Gateway returned 413 at edge. No microservice 10MB errors for those attempts, so it's the edge limit. I can white-list their org for a temporary larger window if they want, but we should recommend a streaming re-architecture.

marie (support): Customer opted to implement chunked NDJSON and retry logic. They'll ship a fix and report back. I've drafted an email with the guidance.

ana (customer-success): :thumbsup: Good work. Follow up if they hit dimension mismatch after switching to the new pipeline.

rohan (eng-ml): One more note: if they use client libraries that batch automatically (e.g., the JS SDK can auto-batch), they should verify the effective payload size produced by the SDK. Sometimes hidden batching + NDJSON can create unexpectedly large requests.

marie (support): Closing the thread once customer confirms. Marking internal tasks: platform to check gateway quota (kevin), eng-ml to add dim-check snippet to docs (rohan), support to send guidance and examples (marie).

kevin (eng-platform): I'll follow up on the temporary whitelist option and ping ANA.
